## Summary
- California
  - Threshold: greater than 10^26 FLOPs for frontier models (frontier compute threshold)
  - Instrument/Section: SB 53 / Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act (TFAIA), frontier framework requirements and transparency disclosures
  - Effective date: January 1, 2026 (core obligations take effect; ongoing framework/reporting follows)

- New York
  - Threshold: greater than 10^26 FLOPs (compute-based trigger) with initial compute-cost trigger; planned amendments replace compute-cost triggers with a $500 million revenue trigger mirroring California
  - Instrument/Section: RAISE Act (S 6953-B) – Frontier Model Disclosure (as enacted; amendments to align with CA forthcoming)
  - Effective date: framework/applicability beginning in 2026; amendments anticipated January 2026 with alignment to CA; enforcement horizon extending toward 2027 per amendment discussions

- European Union
  - Threshold: 10^25 FLOPs presumption for frontier/general-purpose models (rebuttable)
  - Instrument/Section: EU AI Act + General-Purpose AI Code of Practice (CoP) and GPAI governance provisions
  - Effective date: compliance groundwork around August 2, 2025; enforcement possible from August 2, 2026 (varies by jurisdiction and adoption of the CoP)

Which threshold captures the largest number of announced training runs?
- The EU threshold of 10^25 FLOPs would capture more frontier-model trainings than California’s 10^26 FLOPs or New York’s compute-based threshold (even with New York’s planned revenue-trigger alignment). Under typical interpretations, the EU 1e25 threshold is the lowest among the three, thus encompassing the greatest number of announced training runs.

Comparison table
- Jurisdiction | Threshold (FLOPs) | Legal Instrument and Section | Effective Date
- California | > 10^26 FLOPs | SB 53 / Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act (TFAIA) | 2026-01-01
- New York | > 10^26 FLOPs (with compute-cost trigger; planned shift to $500M revenue trigger) | RAISE Act (S 6953-B) – Frontier Model Disclosure (amendments to align with CA) | 2026 (framework/application); amendments anticipated early 2026; enforcement horizon toward 2027
- European Union | > 10^25 FLOPs (rebuttable) | EU AI Act + General-Purpose AI Code of Practice (CoP) and GPAI governance provisions | groundwork 2025-08-02; enforcement possible 2026-08-02

Notes:
- California imposes public disclosures, reporting, governance, and whistleblower protections for frontier AI developers, with large developers defined by revenue ($500 million) for intensified obligations.
- New York signals alignment with California, with amendments to shift from compute-cost triggers to a revenue-based threshold; framework includes oversight and penalties, with 2027 enforcement horizon per amendment discussions.
- The EU relies on a lower presumption threshold (10^25 FLOPs) under GPAI/CoP, with phased groundwork in 2025 and potential enforcement from 2026, varying by member state adoption.
